Projects

Changing Play

2014 - ongoing
Free
About Projects Resources Art + Ideas Archive

Changing Play is an ongoing partnership between Serpentine Education and the Portman Early Childhood Centre that brings together artists, children, parents, and educators to address issues impacting families with young children.

   

The Portman Early Childhood Centre serves children and families in North West London through a multi-agency approach, integrating early education with mental health support, ESOL classes, ante-natal and post-natal services, citizens and housing advice amongst many others. Over the last decade Serpentine Education has commissioned artists to collaborate with children, parents and workers at the Centre. Through embedded, long-term creative processes families and early years workers identify and respond to pressing social issues and work towards collective change. The programme celebrates and uplifts the creativity and resilience of families as they navigate austerity measures, hostile environment policies and an ableist education system. Tools developed in these projects are shared through workshops, forums, films, toolkits, and publications.

Changing Play builds on Serpentine’s commitment to exploring the role of artists in society, asking what possibilities can emerge from sustained, genuine engagement with the everyday realities, struggles, hopes, and dreams of young children and their families.

Changing Play Projects

Everyday Resistance (2018-24) by Jasleen Kaur in collaboration with parents from the Portman, addresses the politics of mothering in the hostile environment. Centering the experiences of parents who have recently arrived in the country the group asks how we can create networks of care to support ourselves and others.

Like Coming Home (2019-23) by Ed Webb-Ingall and families impacted by the housing crisis, asks critical questions about who makes the rules and decisions about the way we live.

Which Way Now? (2018-ongoing) by Sam Curtis in collaboration with children aged three and four, centres the practice of child-led walks to bring children and the local neighbourhood closer in dialogue.

Rights to… (2017-19) by Emma McGarry and Adam JB Walker in collaboration with children and parents from the Centre, looks at why and how neurodiverse and disabled students are being failed by schools.

Who Cares? (2017-19) by Adelita Husni-Bey brings together care-takers and care workers to ask how we can care for each other when the systems of care are being dismantled all around us.

On What Grounds (2017-19), a collaborative project by Bahbak Hashemi-Nezhad and children from the Portman, advocates for children’s right to play beyond the limitations of formal playgrounds. The project raises a critical question: Where are the spaces for children in the city?

Play as Radical Practice (2016-18) Albert Potrony collaborates with children under 5 and early years practitioners, to explore the potential of play and its increasing marginalisation in the education system.

Shapes (2014-2018) by Invisible Spaces of Parenthood with the Portman, highlights the undervaluation of early years practice and the importance of state-maintained nursery schools in an era of government cuts.

About Portman Early Learning Centre

The Portman Early Childhood Centre provides education, care and family support services for young children and their families living in the Church Street area of Westminster, North London. These include a nursery school, adult education classes, family support, employment services, parenting groups and workshops.
